content.title: About
content.content: Fried mushrooms are selected caps of edible mushrooms quickly sautéed in vegetable oil until golden and crisp. They have a rich aroma, crunchy texture and a slightly nutty flavor. The product is ready to eat and works as a snack or as an ingredient in salads, pastas and Asian‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mushrooms are a good source of protein, fiber and B‑vitamins, making them nutritionally valuable.
Frying creates aromatic compounds that enhance flavor compared with raw mushrooms.
More than 30 mushroom varieties are suitable for frying; the most common are button, oyster and honey mushrooms.
Fried mushrooms are often used in vegetarian cuisine as a meat‑like substitute because of their “meaty” texture.
In Russia, fried mushrooms are traditionally served with vinegar or soy sauce.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Mushrooms contain polyphenols and selenium, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Beta‑glucans found in mushrooms stimulate the immune system.

items.title: Contains vitamin D
items.content: When exposed to sufficient UV light, mushrooms can synthesize vitamin D, important for bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie protein source
items.content: One cup of fried mushrooms provides about 3 g of protein while remaining low in fat.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The fiber in mushrooms promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Mushroom allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions ranging from skin rash to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When salt or soy sauce is added, sodium levels can rise; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Those with a sensitive stomach may experience discomfort due to the high fiber content.

items.title: Potential toxins
items.content: Certain wild mushrooms contain toxins; only cultivated, verified varieties should be used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried mushrooms can be enjoyed as a snack, tossed into salads, mixed with pasta, rice or noodle dishes, used as a filling for pies and pizza, or served with soy sauce, garlic mayo or vinegar.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fried mushrooms in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in bags for up to 3 months. Discard any that develop off‑odors, mold or slime.
